mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which lowers borrowing costs and increases consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with declines in FEDFUNDS during periods of monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when UNRATE is below 4%, indicating a mismatch between labor market strength and equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) combined with rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong demand in the housing and retail sectors, which may boost the overall economy and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative despite simultaneous increases in HOUST and RSAFS, indicating no positive relationship between these demand indicators and equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during a period of economic expansion signals increased economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative despite an increase in INDPRO during an economic expansion, indicating no positive relationship between industrial production growth and equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative following an increase in PAYEMS, indicating no immediate positive impact of employment growth on equity markets.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which may lead to higher corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative despite GDPC1 growth exceeding 3%, indicating no positive relationship between GDP growth and equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a supportive monetary policy environment, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative despite low FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE, indicating no positive impact of these monetary conditions on equity markets.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during the early stages of an economic recovery indicates improving consumer confidence and demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative despite an increase in HOUST during early-cycle recovery, indicating no positive relationship between housing starts and equity returns in this regime.
